assessmentSummary.identity: Hands-elevated horizontal push-up using a stable surface; surface height changes external demand without changing the core movement identity.
assessmentSummary.loadInterpretation: Do not assign one fixed body-mass percentage. Hand load varies with surface height, body dimensions, position in the repetition, and tempo.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Use surface height as the primary regression/progression variable. Preserve range, whole-body alignment, scapular motion, and target RPE before lowering the surface.

claims: The hands are elevated on a stable bench or surface.
Elevation reduces pressing demand and supports progression toward a floor push-up.
The exercise is a beginner horizontal pressing pattern using body mass and an elevated support.
The stable elevated surface is an equipment and setup attribute, not a different primary movement pattern.

evidence.sourceTitle: A predictive model for vertical ground reaction force during incline push-ups
claims: Body mass, incline angle, and movement tempo influence vertical ground-reaction force.
Individual body mass and execution conditions should be retained when prescribing intensity.

evidence.sourceTitle: Shoulder electromyography activity during push-up variations: a scoping review
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: Push-up variants recruit shoulder and scapular musculature, with activation affected by variation and support conditions.
Incline evidence is more limited than evidence for standard push-ups, so precise muscle-activation claims should remain conservative.

evidence.sourceTitle: The effect of position on the percentage of body mass supported during traditional and modified push-up variants
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: Upper-extremity load changes between the top and bottom of a push-up.
Difficulty should not be inferred from exercise name alone.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Youth should begin with manageable resistance, learn correct technique, and progress gradually.
Training variables should be adjusted to experience and objective with adequate recovery.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Training and Long-Term Athletic Development
claims: Progressive movement competency and foundational strength precede more demanding loading.
Coaching and progression should be developmentally appropriate.

evidence.sourceTitle: Push-Ups vs. Bench Press Differences in Repetitions and Muscle Activation between Sexes
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
claims: Push-ups can be treated as a quantifiable resistance exercise rather than a generic conditioning movement.
Relative external demand and repetition capacity should both inform dosage.
The exercise requires a stable elevated surface that will not slide or tip under forward and downward force.
Support height and available clear floor space constrain setup and the attainable loading range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Resistance-training dosage should be selected from the athlete's training age, movement competency, objective, and recovery capacity.
Load or difficulty should progress gradually after correct technique can be maintained.
Set the hands slightly wider than shoulder width on an elevated surface and place the feet to form an inclined straight-body position.
Lower the chest toward the support with whole-body alignment, then press to the start without losing trunk position.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Training and Long-Term Athletic Development
claims: Athletes benefit from developmentally appropriate language, visible success criteria, and a progression that preserves movement competency.
The card should explain that raising the support is a valid load adjustment rather than a failed repetition.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Performance and Fitness—Strength and Conditioning Information for Parents
claims: Qualified supervision, clear technique instruction, and appropriate program administration are core safety controls for youth resistance training.
Coaches should observe alignment and range, adjust support height before form failure, and avoid treating all athletes as having the same relative load.
Support elevation makes the pressing task more manageable than a floor push-up for many beginners.
Surface height can be individualized in small steps while retaining the exercise's core identity.

evidence.sourceTitle: Shoulder electromyography activity during push-up variations: a scoping review
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: Support conditions and push-up variations can materially change muscular demand.
Alternate classification should distinguish simple dosage or setup modifiers from changes in laterality, support, and movement demand.
